page.layout: One page of running text in a single column, with no marginal notes. Catchword at the lower right. The right edge shows part of the facing page, which is not transcribed. Faint show-through is at the lower left and is excluded.

main_text.p: certè LENITAS & CONSTAN-TIA non omittentur, illustria sidera in illo virtutum choro. Non fuit à natis regibus (te Fides & Veritas appello) qui magis propriè hæc sibi vindicauerit: & addo ab illis fontibus scaturiginem, se-datum regimen & quietum. Ut guber-nator in magnâ naui flectit & regit om-nia paruo motu. quid ad minuta eo? ut ipse mundi ille rector Deus, machinam hanc quatit & mouet, ipse inconcussus: talis tuus ille genitor, vetus regnandi & securus. Tu succede, sed serò (pietas tua hoc postulat:) & illum atque illos nobis redde, quorum sanguinem & partem præfers. Rapitur ad similitudinem suo-rum excellens quæque natura, & simu-lacrum cælestium animorum refert de-cerpta ab ijs aura. En orbe Christianum turbatum bellis aut disidijs: in te ocu-los conijcit, & aliorum aperta inclinatio est, aliorum occultus metus. Quid hæc nisi

page.notes: The page number "3" at the foot is very faint and is read with doubt. The catchword "nisi" is printed at the lower right. The word "fidera" is printed with a long s and is given as "sidera". The forms "ijs", "disidijs" and "conijcit" are kept as printed, since the i/j rule applies only to consonant i/j. The running text opens mid-sentence on the first line, so the paragraph is marked as continued.
